 Nearly 2,000 Self Assessment scams reported
 HMRC is urging Self Assessment customers to stay alert to scams ahead of the 31 January deadline. 
 1,704 Self Assessment scams have been reported to HMRC in the last 12 months, including around 900 linked to a single tax refund scam.
 HMRC received a total of 95,340 reports of suspected scams, in the 12 months to 31 October.
 HMRC is urging people to stay alert to potential scams ahead of the Self Assessment deadline.
 HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) is warning Self Assessment customers to stay alert to scams after receiving 1,704 reports of Self Assessment-related scams.
 In the last 12 months, HMRC received a total of 48,119 reports of scams where fraudsters impersonated the department.
 Criminals often target taxpayers during the Self Assessment filing season when customers are more likely to expect emails, texts and other correspondence about their tax affairs.
 In August 2026, HMRC received around 900 scam reports linked to a single scam. It used emails containing a malicious attachment which directed customers to a fake GOV.UK page designed to steal personal and financial information.
 Victims were told they had an unclaimed tax repayment and were asked to verify their identity and payment details. This information could then be used by fraudsters to access bank accounts or carry out further fraud.
 HMRC took swift action to shut down the fraudulent activity, protecting thousands of other potential victims.
 HMRC is reminding Self Assessment customers to be vigilant and check on GOV.UK whether the email , SMS message or phone call claiming to be from HMRC is genuine. 
 HMRC will never:
 contact customers by email, text or phone to tell them they are due a refund or ask them to claim one
 ask for personal or financial information by email or text message
 leave threatening voicemails about legal action or arrest
 The Self Assessment deadline to file returns and pay any tax owed for the 2025 to 2026 tax year is 31 January 2027. Customers can file securely online on GOV.UK.
 Lucy Pike, HMRC’s Chief Security Officer, yesterday said:
 We know Self Assessment is a prime target for scammers, who use fake tax refund offers to trick people into handing over personal and financial information.
 You can check if contact from HMRC is genuine on GOV.UK before taking any action. Reporting scams helps us shut them down and protect others.
 HMRC has also identified 1,024 cases of HMRC brand infringement in the 12 months to 31 October and removed a total of 8,713 fraudulent websites and 221 phone numbers linked to scam activity.
 Anyone who receives a suspicious message claiming to be from HMRC should forward emails to phishing@hmrc.gov.uk, texts to 60599, or report phone calls on GOV.UK .
 Further information 
 More information about Self Assessment .
 Government scam advice is available on GOV.UK .
 Anyone due a refund can claim it securely via GOV.UK or the HMRC app .
